title: Personal details and home address
purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and full postal address, plus the canton for residents of Switzerland. The pension fund needs these to register the employee, HR needs them to post documents, and the address country decides most later conditions.

stories.title: Personal details for the pension fund registration
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the employee can be registered as an insured person. The registration is rejected when any of these required fields is empty.
stories.priority_reason: All three are required fields of the pension fund registration. Pensionskasse Muster rejects a registration with missing required fields, which blocks the process.

acceptance_criteria.title: Name and date of birth are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee opens the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the first step, 'Personal details'
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name, last name and date of birth, whatever their other answers. They cannot submit the questionnaire while any of the three is empty.

examples.name: Any employee, regardless of later answers

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is a calendar date
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is a full calendar date, shown and recorded as DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.02.1990), as the pension fund registers it.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are recorded once for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the pension fund registration is prepared
acceptance_criteria.then: first name, last name and date of birth are recorded for the pension fund registration as the employee entered them. No later step asks for them again.

stories.title: Complete home address for posting documents
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their full home address: street, house number, postcode, town and country
stories.so_that: HR can post documents to the employee, using the address as one would write it on an envelope
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and states that the address has to be complete. An incomplete address stops documents from reaching the employee.

acceptance_criteria.title: All five address parts are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is in the 'Home address' step of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for street, house number, postcode, town and country. All five are required for every employee, wherever they live, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted while any part is empty.

acceptance_criteria.title: A normal postal address, nothing more
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: only the parts of a normal postal address are asked (street, house number, postcode, town, country), as written on an envelope. The country is given by its English name, e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany", "Liechtenstein".

acceptance_criteria.title: The address is recorded for HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: HR needs to post a document to the employee
acceptance_criteria.then: the complete home address is recorded for HR as the employee entered it.

stories.title: Home address country is the country of residence for later questions
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to count as the employee's country of residence for all later questions
stories.so_that: whether the employee lives abroad (and so is subject to source tax), and in which state of residence, is known without asking again
stories.priority_reason: Living abroad decides source tax liability and the cross-border part of the tariff code. Asking it twice would contradict the ask-once principle.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence is never asked separately
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: later steps need to know where the employee lives (main residence in Switzerland or not, state of residence)
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio takes the home address country as the country of residence. The employee is not asked about residence again.

acceptance_criteria.title: State of residence for source tax follows the address country
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the state of residence for source tax is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: Switzerland gives 'Switzerland', Germany gives 'Germany', Liechtenstein gives 'Liechtenstein', and any other country gives 'Other country'. The cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein are specified in the cross-border section.

acceptance_criteria.title: Living abroad makes the employee subject to source tax without a nationality question
acceptance_criteria.given: the home address country is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides which questions follow
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee counts as subject to source tax whatever their nationality, and is not asked for nationality, C permit or canton. An employee living in Switzerland is asked for their nationality and canton.

examples.name: Employee living in Germany, e.g. a Swiss citizen like Stefan (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-1a20bb)

stories.title: Canton of residence for employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: employees living in Switzerland to choose their canton from the 26 Swiss cantons
stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the registration can be filled, and employees abroad are not asked a question they have no valid answer to
stories.priority_reason: 'Canton' is a required field of the pension fund registration. A missing value blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton is asked and required only from residents of Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: if the country is Switzerland, the employee is asked for their canton and must answer before submitting. If the country is any other country, the canton is not asked. What the pension fund expects for employees living abroad, and whether 'Canton' means residence or work, is still open (see OQ-canton-abroad, non-blocking).

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton choices are the fund's 26 cantons
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their canton
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich. No other value is accepted. The chosen canton is recorded for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: A canton no longer needed is not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee chose a canton while their address country was Switzerland, and then changed the address country to another country
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton answer is discarded and not recorded. Until submission it may be kept, so switching the country back to Switzerland loses no input.

examples.name: Employee who first entered Switzerland, then corrected to Germany
